climate.overview_html: The headline on September 12 is that the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has officially broken the satellite-era (1966–present) record for latest first hurricane, with zero hurricanes having formed through September 12 — the first time in the modern observation record that no Atlantic hurricane has formed by this date. In parallel, NOAA’s latest extended-range forecast raised the probability of a historically unprecedented El Niño event (3-month ONI ≥+2.5°C, exceeding the 1997–98 and 2015–16 records) to 75%—up from 69% in August—while 15 ensemble members now project Niño 3.4 SST anomalies reaching or exceeding +3.0°C, well above the highest defined intensity category. From the continuing 7-day window: the Nepal–Tibet GLOF confirmed death toll stands at 1,412+ with approximately 5,651+ still missing, with rescue operations continuing; the Mediterranean severe weather outbreak confirmed 2 dead in Italy, 203 mm/24 h rainfall at Lignano Sabbiadoro, and evacuations across Slovenia and Croatia; and the WMO SON 2026 Global Seasonal Climate Update continues to frame near-100% probability of El Niño persistence through DJF, with a co-developing positive IOD at 0.9°C amplifying global teleconnections.

items.headline: 2026 Atlantic Hurricane Season Officially Breaks 60-Year Satellite-Era Record: Zero Hurricanes Through September 12 — First Time in Modern Observation Record; El Niño Shear Unprecedented at Peak of Season; No Tropical Activity Forecast Next 7 Days
items.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has set a new satellite-era record: no hurricane has formed through September 12, the first such occurrence in the period since reliable satellite tracking began in 1966. Previous records were set in 2002 and 2013, both on September 11 — yesterday's digest noted the tie. With NHC forecasting no tropical cyclone development in the Atlantic for at least the next seven days, the record will extend further. Five named storms (Arthur through Edouard) formed but none achieved hurricane strength. The driver is the developing Super El Niño: anomalously strong upper-level westerly winds are producing excessive vertical wind shear across the main development region at the climatological peak of hurricane season. The Eastern Pacific season, running inverse to the Atlantic as expected during El Niño years, has produced 13 named storms, 4 hurricanes, and 2 major hurricanes. If no Atlantic hurricane forms for the remainder of 2026, this would become the first hurricane-free Atlantic season in the satellite era.

items.headline: NOAA El Niño Probability Update: 75% Chance of Record-Breaking Event Exceeding 1997–98 and 2015–16 Peaks (Up From 69% in August); 15 Models Project Niño 3.4 ≥+3.0°C; 97% Probability of Super El Niño Status This Fall–Winter
items.summary: NOAA's most recent extended-range forecast assessment has raised the probability of a historically unprecedented El Niño event — one in which the 3-month ONI equals or exceeds +2.5°C, surpassing both the 1997–98 and 2015–16 records — from 69% (August) to 75% in the September assessment. Fifteen ensemble members now project Niño 3.4 SST anomalies reaching or exceeding +3.0°C, a value with no analogue in the observational record and well above the highest defined El Niño intensity category. The probability of Super El Niño status (ONI ≥+2.0°C) this fall and winter is placed at 97%. Climate scientist Daniel Swain estimates approximately 70% probability that the 2026 event becomes the strongest El Niño since at least 1950, with an expected peak between October and December 2026.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Climate Bulletin: Warmest August on Record at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial — Beats August 2024 by 0.14°C; Completes Hottest Boreal Summer on Record; 2026 Now ~75% Likely to Be Warmest Year in ERA5; SST Hits 21.1°C on August 22
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service August 2026 climate bulletin confirms August 2026 as the warmest August in the ERA5 dataset at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline — beating August 2024 (1.51°C) by 0.14°C. August 2026 completes the hottest boreal summer (June–August) on record globally. Climatologist Zeke Hausfather notes that with eight months in the record, 2026 carries approximately 75% probability of becoming the warmest calendar year in ERA5. Daily global sea surface temperature on August 22 reached 21.1°C — a new record for any August day. The developing Super El Niño adds further thermodynamic fuel to the ongoing temperature trajectory.

items.headline: Carbon Brief State of the Climate September 2026: Strong El Niño Puts 2026 on Track for Second-Warmest Year; August 2026 First Month Since November 2025 to Individually Exceed 1.5°C; 2027 Most Likely to Set New All-Time Record
items.summary: Carbon Brief's September 2026 monthly state-of-the-climate analysis concludes that 2026 is on track to be the second warmest year in the instrumental record, with 2027 the likely candidate for a new all-time record as the Super El Niño's atmospheric warming peak arrives on a 3–6 month lag. August 2026 at 1.65°C was the first individual month since November 2025 to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial, marking a renewed and potentially sustained exceedance. The analysis synthesises forecasts from Copernicus C3S, Berkeley Earth, NOAA, and NASA GISS.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse: Confirmed 1,412+ Dead (1,369 Nepal + 43 Tibet); ~5,651+ Missing; Barrier Lake Risk Ongoing; 5,000+ Rescuers; Debris Recovered 240 km Downstream Inside India
items.summary: The confirmed death toll stands at at least 1,412 as of September 11–12: 1,369 in Nepal and 43 in Tibet. The missing-persons count is approximately 5,651 (5,132 Nepal, 519 Tibet). The disaster originated on August 27 from a glacier collapse on Langtang Lirung at ~5,200 m, generating a seismic signal of Ms 5.2. An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police remain on search operations; approximately 75 foreign nationals, including Americans, remain unaccounted for. No significant toll update was reported on September 12.

items.source: WMO Global Producing Centres / ECMWF / NCEP / JMA
items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: El Niño Deepens to 3.6°C Niño 3.4 Anomaly for September–November; Near-100% Probability Persists Through DJF; Positive IOD Co-Developing at 0.9°C
items.summary: WMO's September 8 Global Seasonal Climate Update for SON 2026 confirms the El Niño deepening on its projected trajectory, with multi-model ensemble forecasts placing the seasonal average Niño 3.4 SST anomaly at approximately 3.6°C for September–November 2026. Near-100% probability is assigned to El Niño persisting through both SON and DJF 2026/27. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) phase is co-developing, with a seasonal mean value of approximately 0.9°C, adding a further global teleconnection amplifier. Both North and South Tropical Atlantic basins are forecast to remain above normal.

weather.overview_html: The key updates on September 12 are in Europe and South Asia. The Mediterranean severe weather outbreak from September 10–11 has moved to post-event damage assessment, with two confirmed dead in Italy — one woman trapped in a flooded underpass at Latisana (Friuli Venezia Giulia) despite a Carabinieri water rescue, and a second killed by broken window glass at Sinalunga (Tuscany) — alongside 203 mm of rainfall in 24 hours at Lignano Sabbiadoro and evacuations across Croatia and Slovenia. In South Asia, Pakistan’s Meteorological Department issued a “final monsoon spell” warning for September 12–17, forecasting heavy to very heavy rain, thunderstorms, and hailstorms across KPK, Gilgit-Baltistan, AJK, Islamabad, and Rawalpindi, with urban flooding risk in Peshawar, Gujranwala, Lahore, and Faisalabad from September 14–17; the season death toll stands at 183. The Atlantic hurricane season officially broke the 60-year satellite-era record with no hurricane formed by September 12; the SE Asia haze emergency and Nepal–Tibet rescue operations continue unchanged.

items.source: The Watchers / Copernicus EMS / ESTOFEX / EUMETSAT
items.headline: Mediterranean Severe Weather Outbreak POST-EVENT: 2 Dead in Italy; 203 mm/24 h at Lignano Sabbiadoro; Flash Flooding Friuli and Liguria; Evacuations Rijeka (Croatia) and Slovenia; Pattern Flip to Flash-Flood Season Now Complete
items.summary: The Mediterranean severe weather outbreak forecast for September 10–11 produced fatal flooding in northern Italy. A woman died at Latisana in Friuli Venezia Giulia after being trapped in a flooded underpass; a Carabinieri officer entered the water and removed her from the vehicle but she died despite the rescue. A second woman was killed by broken window glass at Sinalunga in Tuscany. Rainfall of 203 mm in 24 hours was recorded at Lignano Sabbiadoro and 177 mm at Latisana — extraordinary totals driven by a deep upper trough interacting with record-warm Mediterranean SSTs from the 2026 European heatwave. Flash flooding damaged roads and infrastructure in Liguria and Friuli. Croatia placed emergency services on standby in Rijeka under Orange warnings; evacuations occurred across Slovenia. The event marks the full realisation of the 'flash-flood season' pattern flip that forecasters had warned about throughout August.

items.source: Pakistan Meteorological Department / Pakistan Today / NDMA / PDMA Punjab
items.headline: Pakistan PMD Issues “Final Monsoon Spell” Warning September 12–17: Flash Flood Risk KPK, Punjab, AJK, Islamabad; Urban Flooding Forecast Peshawar, Lahore, Faisalabad September 14–17; Season Death Toll 183
items.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department issued a major alert on September 12, warning of the 'final monsoon spell' — a widespread heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall and hailstorm event expected September 12–17. Flash flood risk is elevated across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Gilgit-Baltistan, Azad Kashmir, Murree, Galiyat, Islamabad, and Rawalpindi. Urban flooding risk is forecast for September 14–17 in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Peshawar, Mardan, Swabi, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot, Faisalabad, and Lahore. Landslides are possible in mountainous areas of KPK, Gilgit-Baltistan, Murree, Galiyat, and Kashmir. NDMA data shows 183 monsoon-related deaths and 515 injured between June 26 and September 11, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa accounting for the highest provincial toll at 74 dead, followed by Punjab (64), Sindh (17), and Azad Kashmir (16). PDMA Punjab placed all district authorities on maximum alert.

items.headline: Atlantic Basin: Zero Tropical Activity Forecast Through Late September; Season Officially Breaks 60-Year Record; El Niño Shear Unprecedented at Seasonal Peak; Eastern Pacific 13 Named Storms / 4 Hurricanes (Inverse Seesaw Pattern Confirmed)
items.summary: NHC has no tropical cyclone forecast for the Atlantic for at least the next seven days as of September 12. The season has produced five named storms but zero hurricanes — a new satellite-era record. The 2026 Super El Niño is creating anomalously strong upper-level westerly shear across the tropical Atlantic at the exact climatological peak of hurricane season. The inverse basin seesaw is active: the Eastern Pacific has 13 named storms, four hurricanes, and two major hurricanes — the standard El Niño pattern. Climatologists note that even if an Atlantic hurricane forms in October–November, the suppression of September activity represents one of the most striking El Niño atmospheric teleconnections ever observed during peak season.

items.source: ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre / Channel NewsAsia / Euronews
items.headline: SE Asia Haze: ASEAN Level 3 Transboundary Haze Alert Remains Active (Since August 26); ~300,000 ha Active Fires Kalimantan; Serian (Sarawak) State of Emergency Continuing; 1.4 Million Malaysian Students in Remote Learning; Below-Normal Rainfall Forecast Through October
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Level 3 transboundary haze alert, first issued August 26, remains in force as of September 12. Approximately 300,000 hectares of active fires in Indonesian Kalimantan continue generating dense smoke with PM2.5 concentrations above 500 µg/m³ in parts of Sarawak and Brunei. Serian district's emergency declaration remains active. Malaysia has kept 1.4 million students in remote learning. Indonesia's BNPB has deployed 12,000 personnel and water-bombing aircraft. IQAir forecasts below-normal rainfall across the southern ASEAN region through October, sustaining elevated fire risk through at least the end of Q3 2026.

items.headline: IMD Heavy-to-Very-Heavy Rainfall Alert for East India September 8–11: Well Marked Low-Pressure Area Over Madhya Pradesh; Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh in Heavy Rain Risk Zone; Monsoon 2026 Season Toll Passes 100
items.summary: India's Meteorological Department issued a heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall alert for East India on September 8, covering Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh for a 3–4 day window, driven by a Well Marked Low-Pressure Area over northeast Madhya Pradesh. India's 2026 monsoon season has now claimed more than 100 lives since July. The alert period ended September 11 as the system weakened and moved into the Bay of Bengal.

renewables.overview_html: The major new transaction on September 11 is Excelsior Energy Capital completing the $760 million sale of its Faraday (682 MW DC, Utah County, Utah) and Skyhawk (128 MW DC, Obion County, Tennessee) solar plants to Enel Green Power North America — approximately 810 MW DC / 625 MW AC combined. Faraday is backed by a 20-year PPA with PacifiCorp and supplies Meta’s energy offset requirements; Skyhawk carries a long-term PPA with the Tennessee Valley Authority. From the continuing window: India added 16.39 GW of renewable capacity in April–July 2026 with grid-scale battery storage growing faster than generation on a percentage basis; and the IEA’s 2026 energy investment outlook maintains total renewable power investment at $665 billion, with solar alone attracting $365 billion.

items.source: PV Tech / Yahoo Finance / Offshore Source
items.headline: Enel Green Power Acquires Faraday (682 MW DC, Utah) + Skyhawk (128 MW DC, Tennessee) Solar Plants From Excelsior Energy Capital for $760 Million — 20-Year PacifiCorp PPA; Meta Energy-Offset Off-take; TVA Contract
items.summary: Excelsior Energy Capital completed the sale of its two largest U.S. solar assets to Enel Green Power North America for a combined transaction value of $760 million, closing September 11. The Faraday Solar Plant (682 MW DC / 525 MW AC) in Utah County, Utah reached commercial operation in September 2025 under a 20-year power purchase agreement with PacifiCorp; Meta purchases its energy attributes to offset corporate carbon emissions. The Skyhawk Solar Plant (approximately 128 MW DC) in Obion County, Tennessee has been operational since 2023 under a long-term PPA with the Tennessee Valley Authority. Excelsior's Renewable Energy Intermediate Fund I LP sold full interests in both plants; Excelsior Renewable Energy Investment Fund II LP sold its Faraday interest. The deal expands Enel Green Power's U.S. solar portfolio and its position in PJM and TVA service territories.

items.headline: India Clean Power Uptake: 16.39 GW Renewable Capacity Added April–July 2026 (14.33 GW Solar + 2.04 GW Wind); Storage Additions Accelerating Faster Than Generation; FY26–27 Tracking ~50 GW Annual Total
items.summary: India added 16.39 GW of renewable energy capacity in the April–July 2026 period (the first four months of fiscal year 2026–27), comprising 14.33 GW of solar PV and 2.04 GW of wind. Battery energy storage system (BESS) additions are accelerating at a faster percentage pace than either solar or wind. The April–July run rate places India on track for approximately 50 GW of annual renewable additions in FY 2026–27, which would be a record and continue India's trajectory as the third-largest renewable market behind China and the United States.

items.headline: Shell Energy Philippines Signs Second 15-Year PSA With Greenlight Renewables for 120 MWp Phase 2 San Isidro Solar (Leyte) — Total Committed Capacity Now 240 MWp
items.summary: Shell Energy Philippines signed a second 15-year power supply agreement with Greenlight Renewables for an additional 120 MWp sourced from Phase 2 of the San Isidro Solar Power Project in Leyte, energised on July 30, 2026. Combined with Phase 1's agreement, Shell Energy's total committed capacity from the San Isidro project reaches 240 MWp, supplying approximately 100 commercial and industrial customers across the Philippines.

items.headline: Qualitas Energy Acquires Cero Generation’s Core European Platform From Macquarie Asset Management — 5.8 GW Solar Pipeline Across Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, Finland
items.summary: Madrid-based Qualitas Energy completed the acquisition of Cero Generation's core European solar development platform from Macquarie Asset Management, gaining a 5.8 GW pipeline across Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, and Finland. Macquarie is retaining Cero's Nordic operations. Qualitas Energy becomes one of Southern Europe's largest independent solar developers with this transaction, reflecting continued institutional capital appetite for early-to-mid stage EU development platforms under REPowerEU.

items.headline: IEA 2026 Energy Investment Outlook: $665 Billion in Global Renewable Power Investment Forecast; Solar Alone $365 Billion; U.S. Solar Capacity Additions Up 45% YoY in Q2 2026 (11.4 GWdc); Batteries Emerging as Grid-Critical Infrastructure
items.summary: The IEA's 2026 energy investment outlook projects total renewable power investment globally at approximately $665 billion for 2026, with solar PV alone attracting roughly $365 billion. The U.S. solar industry added 11.4 GWdc of new capacity in Q2 2026, a 45% year-over-year increase. Battery energy storage systems are increasingly characterised as critical grid infrastructure in markets with high solar penetration: California, Germany, South Australia, Texas, and the UK have all seen strong utility-scale battery growth in 2026.

items.headline: Google, MN8 Energy, and Eos Energy Sign Round-the-Clock PPA: 86 MW Solar + 70 MW/280 MWh Lithium-Ion + 10 MW/100 MWh Zinc Long-Duration Storage on Reclaimed West Virginia Coal Mine
items.summary: MN8 Energy, Eos Energy Enterprises, and Google announced a collaboration to deliver clean, around-the-clock power to the PJM grid from a reclaimed coal mine site in West Virginia. The project pairs 86 MW of utility-scale solar with 70 MW/280 MWh of lithium-ion storage (operational 2029) and 10 MW/100 MWh of Eos's proprietary Z3™ zinc-based long-duration energy storage (operational 2030). Google will purchase energy, capacity, and clean energy attributes under a long-term PPA to support its West Virginia data centre. This represents one of the first commercial-scale deployments of grid-connected zinc LDES alongside lithium-ion in a U.S. renewable project.

science.overview_html: The newest paper in the window is arXiv:2609.11696 (September 10): a head-to-head stress-test of dynamical (WRF) versus generative diffusion-model downscaling for subseasonal extreme precipitation at up to 3-week lead times, finding that WRF edges the diffusion model on a multicell non-stationary event while the diffusion model outperforms WRF on a stationary supercell event — with both substantially improving on raw ECMWF. The result is directly relevant operationally: the September 10–11 Mediterranean outbreak, where 203 mm/24 h was recorded and two people died, is exactly the type of convective extreme precipitation event these methods target. The broader window continues to be defined by WeatherNext 3 (Google DeepMind, arXiv:2609.03582): the first global AI model ingesting live geostationary satellite data and raw station observations at 0.1°/hourly resolution with state-of-the-art probabilistic skill; EastAsiaClimateExtremes (arXiv:2609.08241): the AI-ready S2S benchmark for East Asian atmospheric and oceanic extremes, co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcasts; CloudCast v2 extending ML cloud-cover forecasting to 12-hour lead times at 4-km/15-minute resolution — a direct input to solar dispatch; and the ECMWF AI Weather Quest conclusion with 42 teams, where the winning submission beat ECMWF’s own S2S ensemble.

items.source: arXiv / Bjerknes Centre for Climate Research / University of Bergen
items.headline: arXiv 2609.11696: Stress-Testing Dynamical (WRF) vs Generative Diffusion-Model Downscaling for Subseasonal Extreme Precipitation at 3-Week Lead Times — WRF Wins on Multicell Non-Stationary Events; Diffusion Model More Consistent Across Metrics; Both Beat Raw ECMWF
items.summary: This paper evaluates WRF dynamical downscaling head-to-head against a diffusion-based deep generative model by downscaling ECMWF subseasonal forecasts for two physically distinct extreme precipitation events at lead times up to 3 weeks. Both approaches substantially improve on raw ECMWF outputs. WRF achieves the highest probabilistic skill for a multicell, non-stationary event (similar in character to the September 10–11 Mediterranean outbreak), where the dynamical core's explicit physics captures large-scale forcing. The diffusion model is more consistent across performance metrics and outperforms WRF on a more stationary supercell event, suggesting generative downscaling has an advantage in convection-dominated scenarios where training data provides stronger statistical priors than explicit physics. The study motivates ensemble or regime-adaptive downscaling frameworks rather than a single fixed approach for operational extreme precipitation prediction.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind’s Hourly 0.1° Global AI Weather Model Achieves New State-of-the-Art Probabilistic Skill by Ingesting Live Geostationary Satellite Data — Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and train on raw weather station observations — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based ERA5 initial conditions. It generates new forecasts every hour at 0.1° (~11 km) spatial resolution. On both probabilistic (CRPS) and deterministic skill score benchmarks across the full 10-day medium range, WeatherNext 3 establishes a new state-of-the-art for probabilistic global AI weather forecasting. Deployed in production inside Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, BigQuery, and Earth Engine.

items.source: arXiv / Fudan University / ECMWF / Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.headline: arXiv 2609.08241 (EastAsiaClimateExtremes): First AI-Ready Weekly Benchmark Dataset for East Asian Atmospheric and Oceanic Extremes — AHT, Heavy Rainfall, Marine Heatwaves; Co-Registered With ECMWF S2S Hindcasts; Open on GitHub
items.summary: EastAsiaClimateExtremes is an open benchmark dataset providing ERA5/OISST reanalysis-based weekly extreme labels for anomalously high temperature (AHT), heavy rainfall (HR), and marine heatwaves (MHW) over East Asia, co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcast outputs. The dataset enables direct comparison between AI model predictions and dynamical model subseasonal forecasts, addressing a critical gap: event-based AI-ready datasets for East Asia remain sparse at the subseasonal timescales where dynamical models face their largest skill gaps.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03763 (CloudCast v2): AI Cloud Cover Forecasting Extended From 1–3 h to 12 h Lead Time at 4-km / 15-Minute Resolution, Trained on Copernicus CERRA Reanalysis — Competitive With NWP to 8 h; Direct Input to Solar Dispatch
items.meta: Nielsen, Bjørk, Dittmer et al. (DTU / DMI) · arXiv:2609.03763 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: CloudCast v2 extends ML cloud-cover nowcasting to 12-hour lead times at 15-minute temporal resolution and 4-km spatial resolution, trained on the Copernicus European Regional Reanalysis (CERRA). It achieves skill competitive with NWP to approximately 8-hour lead times on continuous cloud fraction, and substantially outperforms NWP at 1–4 hours on rapid cloud evolution metrics. Cloud cover is the primary driver of solar irradiance forecast error at sub-day timescales, making 12-hour ML cloud forecasting a direct input to solar energy dispatch and grid balancing.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.04427: Input Data Sensitivity in Deep-Learning Hail Nowcasting — More Training Data Beats Architecture Changes; Dual-Pol Radar and Lightning Improve Skill; Radar Reflectivity Alone Insufficient for Large-Hail Discrimination
items.meta: Pacey, Miralles, Hamann, Martius (Univ. Bern / MeteoSwiss) · arXiv:2609.04427 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This paper systematically evaluates how input data choices affect deep-learning hail nowcasting skill without changing model architecture. Adding dual-polarisation radar variables (ZDR, KDP, ρhv) and lightning stroke-density layers each improve skill more than architectural changes alone. Radar reflectivity alone is insufficient for discriminating large-hail (≥2 cm) from ordinary convective precipitation. The study uses a Swiss dataset of 6 hail seasons. Directly relevant to the September 10–11 Mediterranean outbreak, where hail up to 10 cm was forecast.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest: First Year Concludes — 42 Teams From 30+ Countries; DJF 2025/26 Hindcast Challenge Winner Beats ECMWF S2S Ensemble; Annual Awards September 24
items.meta: ECMWF Science Blog · September 2026 · Competition: August 2025–September 2026 · Awards: 24 Sep 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's AI Weather Quest — an international AI/ML sub-seasonal forecasting competition — is concluding its first year with awards scheduled for September 24, 2026. 42 teams from 30+ countries participated, submitting weekly AI-based forecasts for 2-week ensemble temperature and precipitation anomalies globally. The winning DJF 2025/26 hindcast submission outperformed ECMWF's own operational S2S ensemble on the primary skill metric. ECMWF plans to expand the Quest to a second year with longer forecast horizons and a marine heat wave prediction track.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03364: Added Value of Dynamical Downscaling in Sub-Seasonal Tropical Cyclone Forecasting Over Western North Pacific — GloSea6 Experiments Confirm 20–50 km Resolution Threshold for TC Genesis Fidelity
items.meta: Kim et al. (Korea Meteorological Administration) · arXiv:2609.03364 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This study evaluates tropical cyclone representation in sub-seasonal forecasts using GloSea6 over the western North Pacific. Experiments find a critical resolution threshold near 20–50 km below which TC genesis frequency and track distributions diverge sharply from climatology. Dynamical downscaling of 100 km forecasts to 25 km with a regional model substantially improves TC genesis fidelity, track probability distributions, and intensity statistics at 2–4 week lead times — supporting operational ensemble downscaling as a bridge between global sub-seasonal models and regional TC guidance.

items.title: WINT Water Intelligence Raises $36 Million Series D to Scale AI-Powered Water Intelligence Globally — LIP Ventures and Inven Capital Co-Lead; 30,000+ Systems Installed; 1.15 Billion Gallons Saved; $100 Million in Water-Damage Losses Prevented in 2025
items.body_html: WINT Water Intelligence, the Israeli AI water-management platform, closed a $36 million Series D on September 9, co-led by LIP Ventures and Inven Capital (a €500 million European climate tech fund backed by CEZ Group), with participation from existing investors Insight Partners and others. Wint’s platform uses AI to detect and prevent water waste and damage in commercial buildings in real time, reaching more than 30,000 installed systems across nearly 600 enterprise customers by end-2025; in 2025 the technology saved 1.15 billion gallons of water and prevented an estimated $100 million in potential water-damage losses across more than 1,300 incidents. The platform is increasingly positioned as a climate adaptation tool for property and casualty insurers and commercial real estate — water damage from extreme-weather-linked moisture intrusion, pipe failure, and flooding is a rapidly rising loss category for portfolios exposed to intensifying precipitation events. This Series D follows a $35 million Series C in 2023 and a $15 million Series B in 2022; total raised is now approximately $105 million. Capital will fund product development and international expansion.

items.title: Perry Weather Raises $110 Million Growth Investment From Silversmith Capital Partners — Hyperlocal Weather Safety Platform Now Covers 3,000+ Organizations; Plans 50+ New Dallas Hires; Total Funding $131 Million
items.body_html: Perry Weather, the Dallas-based hyperlocal weather safety and operations platform, closed a $110 million growth investment on September 9, led by Silversmith Capital Partners, with participation from prior investor Arthur Ventures. The round brings total funding to $131.35 million. Perry Weather pairs purpose-built on-site hardware weather stations with cloud-connected software to deliver real-time hyperlocal monitoring, automated alerts, and AI-assisted siren activation covering lightning, extreme heat, high wind, and air quality across more than 3,000 organizations including school districts, municipal governments, construction firms, manufacturers, and major professional sports leagues. The company plans to add more than 50 new roles through 2027 at its Dallas headquarters and will accelerate AI-powered capability development across its product suite.

items.title: ARC Ride (Kenya) Closes $33.3 Million Series A to Scale Battery-Swapping Electric Motorcycle Network Across Sub-Saharan Africa — IFC, BII, Proparco, Novastar Ventures Lead; 5,000 New E-Motos; Expanding to Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda
items.body_html: Kenyan electric mobility startup ARC Ride closed a $33.3 million financing round on September 8, comprising a $23 million Series A equity round co-led by Novastar Ventures and Norrsken22, alongside a $10 million debt tranche. Strategic investors include the International Finance Corporation (IFC), British International Investment (BII), Proparco, Musashi Seimitsu, and Talanton. ARC Ride operates a Battery-as-a-Service model reducing upfront cost barriers to electric motorcycles and plans to add 5,000 electric motorcycles and expand from Kenya into Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda.

items.title: Howden Re Launches International Alternative Solutions Practice — Dedicated Parametric, ILS, and Climate-Risk Transfer Team; Hire of 12-Person Ex-Aon Reinsurance Team; Focus on Sovereign Nat-Cat, Food Security, and Transition Risk
items.body_html: Howden Re announced the formal launch of its International Alternative Solutions Practice on September 6, a dedicated team focused on parametric reinsurance, Insurance-Linked Securities (ILS), and bespoke climate-risk transfer structures, anchored by a 12-person team predominantly hired from Aon’s reinsurance solutions division. Priority markets include sovereign parametric nat-cat covers for Small Island Developing States and lower-middle-income countries, multi-year food security triggers linked to ENSO indices, and transition-risk liability covers for energy companies managing coal asset retirement. The launch reflects continued growth in demand for ILS-style risk transfer as traditional reinsurance capacity tightens on climate-exposed lines.
items.source_html: Howden Re / Reinsurance News

items.title: Nexeon (UK) Closes £100 Million Series D for Silicon Anode Battery Materials — National Wealth Fund and Honda Xcelerator Lead; Expands Teesside Pilot Facility Targeting 10,000-Cycle EV Battery Longevity
items.body_html: Abingdon-based Nexeon closed a £100 million Series D round on September 6, led by the UK’s National Wealth Fund (through UKIB) and Honda Xcelerator Ventures, with Korea Development Bank as strategic co-investor. Nexeon’s silicon anode technology replaces or supplements graphite in EV battery anodes, increasing energy density by up to 20% and targeting cycle lives exceeding 10,000 full charge-discharge cycles — critical for next-generation BEV commercial vehicles and long-duration residential storage. Funds will expand Nexeon’s Teesside pilot facility and accelerate scale-up toward a gigawatt-hour-scale manufacturing line. Honda’s participation follows a multi-year joint development agreement.

items.title: Swiss Re: Data Centers and AI Workloads Create $200 Billion Premium Opportunity for Insurers Through 2030 — Hyperscaler Power Demand to Triple; Nat-Cat Exposure in Low-Risk Corridors; Cyber-Physical Risk Convergence Identified as Major Coverage Gap
items.body_html: Swiss Re Institute’s September 2026 sigma report quantifies data centres and AI compute infrastructure as a $200 billion cumulative premium opportunity for the global (re)insurance industry through 2030. The report projects that hyperscaler power demand will triple by 2030, creating new concentrations of physical risk exposure at a scale substantially exceeding existing commercial insurance penetration. Swiss Re identifies cyber-physical risk convergence as the major emerging coverage gap: a single data centre outage can trigger simultaneous property damage, business interruption, and downstream liability claims across multiple policyholders. Nat-cat exposure is flagged: many hyperscaler campuses in historically low-risk corridors (Iowa, Virginia, Texas) face rapidly changing flood, heat, and severe-thunderstorm risk profiles. Swiss Re recommends parametric trigger structures and real-time physical risk monitoring as components of a new data-centre risk transfer framework.
items.source_html: Swiss Re Institute / Reuters

items.title: Light (PoweredbyLight) Raises $46 Million Series A Led by Matrix Partners to Scale “Embedded Electricity” Platform — Enables Any Company to Offer Branded Retail Electricity With Built-In VPP Participation; Covers 30% of U.S. Residential Solar Sales
items.body_html: Light (brand: PoweredbyLight), an Austin-based platform letting any company become a regulated retail electricity provider via API — including licensing, wholesale procurement, billing, customer support, and virtual power plant (VPP) participation — closed a $46 million Series A led by Matrix Partners with participation from Activate Capital, Spark Capital, Mischief, Gigascale Capital, MCJ, and BoxGroup. Total funding now exceeds $60 million; the partner network covers more than 30% of all U.S. residential solar sales and 500,000+ homeowners; in H1 2026, 100% of new electricity brands entering Texas ERCOT launched on Light’s platform.
